pages.name: Which way?
pages.task: A torch beam strikes a flat mirror at a slant. Which way does it leave?
pages.answer: At the same slant, tipped the other way
pages.why: A mirror sends light off at the same slant it arrives at. It leaves on the other side of the line square to the mirror.

pages.name: From the normal
pages.task: A beam strikes a mirror at 25° to the mirror's surface. What is the angle of reflection?
pages.why: The normal is at 90° to the surface. So the beam arrives 90 − 25 = 65° from the normal. It leaves at the same 65° on the other side.

pages.name: Follow the target
pages.task: A torch beam reflects off a mirror onto a target. The target moves 30° round the mirror. How far must you turn the mirror to keep the beam on it?
pages.why: Turning the mirror by an angle turns the beam by twice that angle. So the mirror turns half of 30°. That is 15°. Turned 15°, the mirror puts the beam back on the target.

pages.name: Find the image
pages.task: A lamp stands in front of a mirror. An eye looks in from one side. Where does this eye see the lamp's image?
pages.answer: Behind the mirror, straight across from the lamp, as far back
pages.why: The eye traces the reflected ray straight back. The angles are equal, so that line passes through one spot for any eye. The spot is straight across the mirror from the lamp. It is as far behind as the lamp is in front.

pages.name: The periscope
pages.task: A periscope's mirrors are 2 m apart. An object is 30 m from the top mirror, and your eye is 0.1 m from the lower mirror. How far away does the object's image look?
pages.why: The top mirror puts a first image 30 m behind it. That image is 30 + 2 = 32 m from the lower mirror. So the lower mirror puts the final image 32 m behind itself. Your eye is 0.1 m in front of that mirror. So the image looks 32 + 0.1 = 32.1 m away.

pages.name: A knocked mirror
pages.task: A periscope's top mirror is knocked 2° off its 45°. How far off vertical does it now send the light down?
pages.why: The light arriving is still level. Turning the mirror 2° changes the angle to the normal by 2° on the way in and 2° on the way out. So the light it sends down turns 2 × 2 = 4° off vertical.
